headline: Ether has held a small floor near $2,061 for 35 minutes; with a wider $21 safety exit the trade pays about 1.7 to 1 if it works as planned.

messages.text: Final word. The Judge was right that a $14 exit is too tight when a normal one-hour swing is about $20. I widened it: buy near $2,068, get out at $2,047 (a $21 risk, about one normal hour of wiggle).

messages.reply_to: Bear: Ether is still under every important average line
messages.text: True, and I will not hide it: the trend is still down on every chart. That is why this is a small bounce trade, not a bet that the drop is over. I only need price to climb back to its day-average of about $2,096.

messages.reply_to: Bear: the bounce is happening on very thin trading
messages.text: Thin trading is fair. But after the big $2,028 plunge, seven candles in a row (35 minutes) dipped no lower than $2,061 and none went back toward $2,028. A floor that holds that long is real, though still young.

Honest math from $2,068 with the $2,047 exit: first target $2,096 wins $28 (about 1.3 to 1). Second target $2,113 wins $45 (about 2.1 to 1). Selling half at each, the average win is about $36 for $21 risked, so roughly 1.7 to 1.

The risk is clear: if $2,061 breaks and $2,047 is hit, you lose about $21 and that is the end of it. I think a bounce from a flushed-out low is more likely than not to reach the first target, so the odds are worth taking small.

argument:
Fresh data (14:01 UTC): ETH 2068.78-2069.17, 5m RSI 35.2, 15m RSI 30.1, 1h RSI 27.7, 1h ATR14 19.86, 5m ATR14 9.93. The Judge flagged that the Round 2 stop (2054, risk 14) was about 0.67x the 1h ATR. I have widened it. New stop 2047: risk 21 from an entry of 2068, which is about 1.06x the 1h ATR and 2.1x the 5m ATR, and it sits 14 under the 2061 base lows, with the 2028 flush low still a further 19 below. A close under 2061 would show the base failed; 2047 is where I accept being wrong.

Strongest remaining Bear point: price is below EMA9/EMA21/SMA50/SMA200 on 5m, 15m and 1h, the 1h MACD histogram keeps widening (-3.79 vs -3.08), and volume since the flush is thin (5m 0.1x average). I accept all of that. The response is trade design: the long is a mean-reversion scalp to VWAP (2095.93) and the 1h EMA21 (2109.12), not a trend trade. After the 13:30 flush (volume 35,566 vs 760-1,500 before) the following 7 five-minute candles have lows 2061.16, 2061.11, 2063.32, 2068.09, 2063.72, 2065.51, i.e. no retest of 2028. Funding is +0.0026%, so longs are not crowded.

Honest reward-to-risk with entry 2068, stop 2047 (risk 21): T1 2096 = +28 (1.3:1), T2 2113 = +45 (2.1:1), T3 2132 (15m recent high 2132.07) = +64 (3.0:1). Plan: sell half at T1, half at T2, and move the stop to entry after T1. Blended outcome if T1 and T2 both fill: about +36.5 average, 1.7:1. If only T1 fills and the rest stops at entry: +14 on the full size, 0.7:1. Admitted weaknesses: the base is only about 35 minutes old, volume is thin, the order book is noisy (0.84 now, 1.19 and 2.07 earlier), and ETF flows have been negative.

evidence.claim: Price 2068.78; EMA9 < EMA21 and price below SMA50 and SMA200 on 5m, 15m and 1h; 1h MACD histogram -3.79 (prev -3.08)
evidence.plain: The overall trend is still down on every chart, and the hourly sell push is still growing. This is why I treat the trade as a short bounce only.

evidence.claim: After the 13:30 5m flush (low 2028.32, close 2066.12, volume 35,566), the next 7 5m candles had lows 2061.16, 2061.11, 2063.32, 2068.09, 2063.72, 2065.51; latest close 2069.17
evidence.plain: Price has not gone back near the $2,028 bottom for 35 minutes. Dips keep stopping around $2,061, a small floor.

evidence.claim: 1h ATR14 19.86; 5m ATR14 9.93; stop 2047 is 21 below entry 2068
evidence.plain: ATR is the size of a normal swing. A normal one-hour swing is about $20, so a $21 exit is wide enough not to be hit by ordinary wiggles.
evidence.source: market_data.py live re-run (Binance); arithmetic by Bull

evidence.claim: Session VWAP 2095.93; 1h EMA21 2109.12; 1h SMA20 2113.68; 15m recent high 2132.07
evidence.plain: These are the nearby 'ceilings' price has to climb to: the day's average price, then a cluster around $2,110, then $2,132.

evidence.claim: Perp funding rate +0.0026%; Fear and Greed 32 (Fear), up from 29; 24h low 2028.32
evidence.plain: Few people are piling into risky long bets, and the fear score is slightly improving, so there is no crowded-buyer overhang to unwind.

evidence.claim: Order book top-100 bid/ask ratio 0.84 now (earlier 0.69, 1.19, 2.07)
evidence.plain: This number jumps around every minute, so I am not using it as a reason to buy.

rebuttals.opponent_point: Bear: price is below every moving average and 1h downside momentum is still growing
rebuttals.response: Accepted. The trade is a mean-reversion bounce to VWAP 2096 and the 1h EMA21 2113, sized small with a 21-point stop, not a trend reversal call.

rebuttals.opponent_point: Bear: the bounce is on thin volume (5m 0.1-0.4x)
rebuttals.response: Accepted as a weakness. Offsetting fact: seven candles have held above 2061 and none revisited 2028. If 2061 fails, the 2047 stop exits for a loss of about 21.

rebuttals.opponent_point: Bear: risk 49 vs reward 25 from the old 2022 stop
rebuttals.response: That applied to the old plan. The final plan risks 21 for 28/45/64, blended about 1.7:1 on a half-and-half exit.

plan.risk_reward: 1.3:1 to T1, 2.1:1 to T2, 3.0:1 to T3; about 1.7:1 blended selling half at T1 and half at T2

plan_plain: Buy around $2,068. If price falls to $2,047, sell and accept a loss of about $21 per Ether. Sell half at $2,096 (win about $28) and move your exit up to your entry price; sell the rest at $2,113 (win about $45), or $2,132 if it keeps going. If both halves hit, you win about $1.70 for each $1 you risked. If only the first target hits, the gain is smaller than the risk, so this trade needs a bounce to keep going.
